name: Approach B — "Drawer + contextual header" incremental retrofit (mockup)
description:
OBJECTIVE
Build a functional HTML mockup of mobile strategy B for the codx-junior web client: the cheapest path that still removes the "no navigation" defect.

APPROACH B (to be prototyped)
Keep the current model (single-mode routes + the existing sidebar) but fix it at the shell level and add only the chrome a phone needs:
- A shared, thin mobile app bar rendered once by the shell (src/App.vue): hamburger on the left (always visible — this is the fix for the unreachable drawer), current screen title, project switcher + notifications + avatar on the right.
- The existing DesktopSidebar becomes a proper left drawer: overlay + slide-in, grouped sections (Apps, Workspaces, More), full-height, scrollable, closes on selection.
- No bottom tab bar. Navigation stays discoverable through the drawer plus a small "recent screens" strip at the top of the drawer.
- Each screen keeps its own content but is wrapped by one shared page container that provides scroll, padding and a header slot; screens without a header get the app bar title automatically.

REQUIRED SCREENS IN THE MOCKUP (single HTML file, phone frame 390x844, dark theme)
1. Home / management dashboard with the new app bar (hamburger visible).
2. Drawer open over the home screen, grouped as described, with the current screen highlighted.
3. Tasks board opened with the app bar showing a back arrow + title.
4. Chat conversation (fixed composer) with the app bar.
5. Global settings — the screen that today duplicates its desktop aside and mobile drawer: show the flattened single-column version.
Navigations must work with mock data: open/close drawer, open a destination from the drawer, back from Tasks to Home. One self-contained .html file (public CDN libs allowed).

DELIVERABLE PATHS
docs/mobile/strategy-B-drawer.html (self-contained) and docs/mobile/strategy-B-notes.md (max 1 page: what changes in src/App.vue and DesktopSidebar.vue, which screens still need individual work, effort estimate in days as optimistic/likely/pessimistic, top 3 risks).

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
- Visual language must match the current app: daisyUI 5 / Tailwind dark theme, FontAwesome icons.
- This is the low-risk option: prefer surgical changes over redesign. State explicitly in the notes which of the 9 defects of the audit (see the M0 task) this approach does NOT fix.

ACCEPTANCE
- The two files exist, the HTML opens standalone at 390 px with no console errors, all 5 flows work, and the notes contain the explicit "not fixed" list + effort range.
